key_insight: KANs can predict airfoil pressure distributions well and interpolate across conditions, but they do not clearly outperform a well-tuned MLP and trail the best GNN in this study.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs may offer a lower-complexity and faster-training alternative when accurate pressure prediction is needed across Mach number and angle of attack.
method: Compared KANs against MLPs and graph neural networks for airfoil surface pressure prediction.
Tested subsonic and transonic airfoils with interpolation across Mach numbers and angles of attack.
Evaluated predictive accuracy alongside model complexity and training cost.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates predicted pressure coefficients for airfoils across subsonic and transonic regimes, finding KAN performance comparable to but slightly below a suitably trained MLP, with the best accuracy from a GNN.
watch_item: KAN performance is sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and can suffer from training instabilities, so careful optimization is required.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
